characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s, per ASTM E-140-02; average of ten measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate bulk hardness of the alloys in HR, cold rolled and heat-treated conditions

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Supra 55 FEG-Scanning electron microscope equipped with EDS and Nordley EBSD detectors (Oxford); TSL-OIM software
characterization_methods.key_findings: HR 28Mn0Ni: equiaxed austenite grains (d ~5–7 μm), nearly random texture, single-phase austenite (B2-free)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Step size 120 nm (fine-grained) and 250 nm (coarse-grained) over ~100×100 μm² and ~200×200 μm² areas; three scans per sample; polished to colloidal silica ~100 nm finish
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine grain orientations, grain size, twin fraction (Σ3 CSL boundaries), KAM (strain localization) and GOS (recrystallization)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku XRD instrument with Co-Kα radiation at 45 kV and 135 mA, beam size ~2 mm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Co-Kα radiation, 45 kV, 135 mA, beam size ~2 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of the alloys in cold rolled and heat-treated conditions

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Three low-density steel grades with different Mn and Ni content were prepared by the vacuum induction melting route; the sound portion of the 30 kg ingot was used.
The sound portion of the 30 kg ingot was homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h prior to hot rolling.
Hot rolled at 1323 K to a final plate thickness of about 13 mm; this processing condition is hereafter referred to as HR. The details of the hot rolling process were reported elsewhere [21].
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: final hot rolled plate thickness ~13 mm

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: AFFRI Vickers hardness tester; peak load 30 kg (~300 N); dwell time 15 s; hardness averaged over ten measurements per sample; HR-condition value reported in [21]

defects.type: annealing twins (twin fraction ~28–40%; the higher-Mn LDS alloys contained a higher twin fraction than 15Mn5Ni)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: equiaxed; similar grain sizes among all three alloys

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenitic (γ) low-density steel in the hot rolled (HR) condition; 28Mn0Ni is Ni-free and B2-free. Equiaxed γ-matrix grains with nearly random texture, similar grain size to the other two alloys. Among the three alloys, 28Mn0Ni contained the lowest volume fraction of κ-carbides.

unmapped_findings: In the hot rolled (HR) condition the three LDS alloys (28Mn0Ni, 28Mn5Ni, 15Mn5Ni) exhibited about 20–70% of total tensile elongation to failure at room temperature, with the 15Mn5Ni alloy displaying the lowest ductility (reported in the authors' previous study [21]).
The HR microstructures of all three alloys were reported in a previous study [21] and are used in the present work as the starting condition for cold rolling.

28Mn0Ni in the HR condition is the Ni-free, single-phase austenitic (B2-free) LDS reference material; unlike the Ni-containing alloys it contains no prior B2 phase, which is why it recrystallizes and grain-coarsens faster than the Ni-bearing alloys after cold rolling and heat treatment.
The alloy composition (Table 1) for 28Mn0Ni is Mn 28.3 ± 0.4 wt.%, Al 9.0 ± 0.05 wt.%, C 0.9 ± 0.01 wt.%, Ni not added/detected, Fe balance.
